clue.text: Pawnbroker succeeded given a million in America

parts.note: 'uncle' is old slang for a pawnbroker
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies
the article taken as written, 'given' meaning added on
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A pawnbroker in America did well after being handed a million dollars.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle Sam is the personification of the United States; 'in America' hides the definition behind a phrase that looks like setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Sam is the traditional cartoon figure standing for the US government and nation.

clue.text: More horrible wine Roman fiddler endlessly consumes?

indicators.note: consuming something takes it inside, so one word goes into the other
endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: Emperor Nero reputedly fiddled while Rome burned
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: An emperor guzzling wine while his city burns, which only makes things worse.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastier is the comparative of nasty, meaning more unpleasant or horrible.

clue.text: Charged a lot in Californian city retreat

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: Overpriced in a Los Angeles hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged a lot' reads as overcharging, but means heavily loaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means weighed down with a heavy load, as a charged vessel is filled up.

clue.text: Scrubbed and combed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: cleaned by hard rubbing
second meaning: searched thoroughly through an area

explanation.surface: Someone cleaned up and tidied their hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To scour is both to clean by rubbing hard and to search a place thoroughly.

clue.text: See 27
Grass, about one kilo needed for Hairy Biker

indicators.note: 'about' puts one word around the outside of the others, enclosing them

parts.note: to grass, or sing, is to inform to the police
Roman numeral one
K is the abbreviation for kilo

explanation.surface: A TV cook needs his weekly kilo of weed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' reads as the drug, but it is the verb meaning to inform, as do sing and squeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Si King was one half of the Hairy Bikers, the bearded cookery-show duo on British television.

clue.text: Split for one opening finally concealed in chair?

definitions.note: the '?' marks a definition by example

indicators.note: 'in' places one word inside the other

parts.note: a chair is a seat

indicators.note: the last letter is hidden from view, so it drops out

parts.note: a pore is a tiny opening in the skin

explanation.surface: A question about a split concealed in a chair's seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' looks like a crack, but it is the Croatian port on the Adriatic.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in Croatia is a major harbour city, an example of a port on the sea.

clue.text: Ken's policy expert climbing rock shelf

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a wonk is a policy expert
a ledge is a narrow shelf of rock

explanation.surface: A man named Ken, a policy wonk, scales a cliff ledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ken' looks like a man's name, but it is the noun meaning range of understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Ken means range of understanding, as in 'beyond my ken', which is knowledge.

clue.text: New progressive movement dawning

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
an ascent is movement upwards, progress

explanation.surface: A new progressive political movement is beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means just coming into being, emerging as a day does at dawn.

clue.text: Spent greenbacks when touring Spain?

indicators.note: a tour goes all the way round a place, so one word wraps around another

parts.note: greenbacks are US dollars, code USD
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Someone ran through their dollars while on holiday in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent and used both describe something consumed or exhausted, as a used battery is a spent one.

clue.text: Animal with flower returning another flower for La Scala?

definitions.note: the '?' marks the definition by example

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the letters run right to left

parts.note: a hare is a long-eared animal
a flower is something that flows, a river: the Po in Italy
a second river, the Ouse in England

explanation.surface: Bring an animal and some flowers to decorate La Scala.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' twice means a river, the usual crossword pun on something that flows; the first two pieces together run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: La Scala in Milan is the world's most famous opera house, an example of the class named by the answer.

clue.text: Duke having private meal

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
private as in inner, personal thoughts

explanation.surface: An aristocrat dines alone, away from company.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinner is the main meal of the day, eaten in the evening or at midday.

clue.text: Bear's sure hold that needs breaking

indicators.note: a hold that must be broken has its parts smashed and put back in another order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wrestler pinned in a bear's grip must break free of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal, but it is the verb to carry or take on, as in bearing a burden.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoulder a burden or responsibility is to bear it, taking the weight on yourself.

clue.text: One using C and D three times with guitar playing

definitions.text: One using C and D three times with guitar playing
definitions.note: the whole clue is the definition, read as a user of C, cocaine

indicators.note: playing the letters like notes on an instrument puts them into a fresh order

parts.note: the letter taken as written
three Ds
taken as written

explanation.surface: Reads like a guitarist strumming chords C and D over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: C and D look like chords in a music lesson, but C is slang for cocaine, so the whole clue also describes someone hooked on the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: C is slang for cocaine, so someone using it habitually is an addict of that drug.

clue.text: Lovelorn cowboy on lake shows tactless behaviour

indicators.note: lorn means bereft, so lovelorn here means losing the love letter, zero

parts.note: a gaucho is a South American cowboy
Lake Erie, one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A heartbroken cowboy by the lake behaves clumsily.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is zero in tennis, so the letter O is what the lovelorn cowboy loses.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaucherie is social awkwardness or clumsiness, from French gauche, meaning left-handed.

clue.text: Murder in kitchen regularly ignored

indicators.note: every other letter is ignored at regular intervals, leaving the rest

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A killing in the kitchen that keeps being overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: Ice is slang for kill, chiefly American gangster speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice someone is slang for to kill them, as in gangster films.

clue.text: See 28
Bean curd content of uneaten sandwiches?

indicators.note: the clue words sandwich the answer between them, holding it inside their run of letters

parts.note: found across the end of one word, the next, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A query about what is in the sandwiches someone left uneaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content of' looks like a selection signal, but the run conTENT OF Uneaten holds the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tofu is curd made by pressing soya milk, a staple bean product in East Asian cooking.

clue.text: Folding elegantly, banking system backed mate in Paris

indicators.note: backed means put into reverse, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: giro is a bank transfer system
ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: A Parisian friend elegantly folds while the bank's system goes into reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of folding paper into decorative shapes.

clue.text: Honey in sugary centre

parts.note: sugary food tastes sweet
the heart of something is its centre

explanation.surface: Honey at the middle of a sweet treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Honey' is the food in the surface but a term of endearment in the answer; 'in' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Honey and sweetheart are both affectionate names for a loved one.

clue.text: She leaves hotel — a rising tide brings fish

indicators.note: something that leaves goes away, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
H is hotel in the NATO alphabet
taken as written

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means reading upwards

parts.note: the flow is the incoming tide

explanation.surface: A woman checks out of a hotel as the tide comes in with fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea wolf, or wolf fish, is a large fierce-toothed fish of northern seas.

clue.text: One must yield to Madame in drag bar

indicators.note: to yield to something is to give up a place for it, so one piece swaps out for another

parts.note: to trail is to drag along behind
Roman numeral one
Mme is the abbreviation for Madame

explanation.surface: A performer gives way to a madame in drag at a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drag' and 'bar' suggest a nightclub; drag is to haul and bar is the verb to hinder.
explanation.definitionFit: To trammel is to restrict or hinder, as a bar prevents movement.

clue.text: Rally where Rolls Royce rounds eastern bight

indicators.note: to round something is to go around it, so the outer letters enclose the rest

parts.note: RR is the abbreviation for Rolls Royce
E is eastern
a bight is a bay or cove

explanation.surface: A motor rally where a Rolls Royce drives around a bay in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rally' looks like a car event, but it is the verb to regain strength.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally and to recover both mean to regain health, strength or position after a setback.

clue.text: Centre introducing cut that's wrongly perceived

indicators.note: to introduce is to bring something in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: mid means the centre, as in midway
to shear is to cut, as with sheep

explanation.surface: A misunderstanding about a cut announced at the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Misheard means heard incorrectly, a sound wrongly taken in by the ear.

clue.text: 500 at frozen arena effect hydration

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
an ice rink is a frozen arena

explanation.surface: Five hundred people at an ice arena having an effect on hydration.
explanation.definitionFit: To drink is to bring about hydration by taking in water.

clue.text: Grovelling sailor caught boarding fast plane

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: a passenger boarding goes into the craft, so one letter sits inside the word for it

parts.note: a jet is a fast aircraft
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A sailor bowing and scraping as he is arrested getting on a jet.
explanation.definitionFit: Abject behaviour is utterly servile and self-abasing, exactly what grovelling describes.

clue.text: Tribe's self-defence system incomplete — what a shame!

indicators.note: incomplete means the last letter is missing

parts.note: judo is a martial art of self-defence
an exclamation of sympathy

explanation.surface: A tribe's martial arts falls short, to someone's regret.
explanation.definitionFit: Judah was one of the twelve tribes of Israel, descended from Jacob's son.

clue.text: Sunak bridling at disorder is showing loyalty to state

indicators.note: bridling a horse puts the harness around its head, so one word holds the others

parts.note: Rishi Sunak was UK Prime Minister, PM
taken as written
a riot is public disorder
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister bristles at unrest while flaunting love of country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridling at' reads as taking offence, but bridling encloses, and 'at' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Patriotism is devotion and loyalty to one's own country or nation.

clue.text: Hairy Biker gone has me very sad, distraught

indicators.note: someone distraught is all over the place, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fan mourning a TV favourite admits being upset.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a tribute: the second Hairy Biker died in 2024, and the anagram fodder states the grief.
explanation.definitionFit: Dave Myers, partner of Si King on the Hairy Bikers cookery programmes, died in February 2024.

clue.text: Police show vandalised NY outfield

indicators.note: something vandalised has been smashed up, so these letters are wrecked and rebuilt

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Police put on a display after a New York ballpark is trashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Line of Duty is a BBC television drama about a police anti-corruption unit.

clue.text: Desert, boundless one, devouring goddess devours

indicators.note: without bounds means the outer edges of the word are taken away
to devour is to swallow whole, so one word ends up inside another

parts.note: Kali is the Hindu goddess of destruction, often shown devouring
'one' stands for another desert, the Sahara, here losing its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A desert goddess consumes everything in an endless wasteland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' refers back to 'Desert': another desert, the Sahara, trimmed at both ends, goes inside the goddess Kali.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kalahari is a large semi-arid sandy region in southern Africa, covering much of Botswana.
